hints: Write each minor-segment area as sector area minus triangle area.
For chord $AP$ the central angle is $x$; for chord $BP$ it is $\pi-x$, and $\sin(\pi-x)=\sin x$.
Set the first segment area equal to half the second, cancel $r^2/2$, and rearrange for $x$.
walkthrough:
Recall the formula for the area of a circular segment of radius $r$ subtending an angle $\theta$ at the centre:
$$\text{Area of segment} = \text{Area of sector} - \text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta - \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta)$$

Determine the area of the minor segment on chord $AP$:
The central angle subtended by arc $AP$ is $\angle AOP = x$ radians.
$$\text{Area}(AP) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(x - \sin x)$$

Determine the area of the minor segment on chord $BP$:
Since $AB$ is a straight diameter, the central angle subtended by arc $BP$ is $\angle BOP = \pi - x$ radians.
$$\text{Area}(BP) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\big((\pi - x) - \sin(\pi - x)\big)$$

Use the trigonometric identity $\sin(\pi - x) = \sin x$ to simplify the expression for $\text{Area}(BP)$:
$$\text{Area}(BP) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\pi - x - \sin x)$$

Set up the given geometric condition that $\text{Area}(AP) = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{Area}(BP)$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}r^2(x - \sin x) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\pi - x - \sin x)\right]$$

Divide both sides by the non-zero common factor $\dfrac{1}{2}r^2$:
$$x - \sin x = \dfrac{1}{2}(\pi - x - \sin x)$$

Multiply through by $2$ and rearrange terms to isolate $x$:
$$2(x - \sin x) = \pi - x - \sin x$$
$$2x - 2\sin x = \pi - x - \sin x$$
$$2x + x = \pi - \sin x + 2\sin x$$
$$3x = \pi + \sin x$$
$$x = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi + \sin x)$$

hints: Put the equation from part (i) in zero form, such as $f(x)=3x-\pi-\sin x$.
Calculate $f(1)$ and $f(1.5)$ and show their signs differ; continuity then locates a root between them.
walkthrough:
Define a continuous function corresponding to the equation $3x - \pi - \sin x = 0$:
$$f(x) = 3x - \pi - \sin x$$
(Or equivalently, $g(x) = x - \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi + \sin x)$).

Conclude using the sign change property:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous on $[1, 1.5]$ and $f(1) < 0$ while $f(1.5) > 0$, there is a change of sign.
By the Intermediate Value Theorem, the root $x$ lies in the open interval $(1, 1.5)$.

hints: Use the fixed-point form already established: $x_{n+1}=(\pi+\sin x_n)/3$.
Start with a value from $[1,1.5]$, record each iterate to 5 decimal places, and continue until the values stabilize to 3 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Set up the fixed-point iterative formula derived from part (i):
$$x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi + \sin x_n)$$

Choose an initial value in the interval $[1, 1.5]$, for example $x_1 = 1.25$:
$$x_2 = \dfrac{\pi + \sin(1.25)}{3} \approx 1.36353$$
$$x_3 = \dfrac{\pi + \sin(1.36353)}{3} \approx 1.37340$$
$$x_4 = \dfrac{\pi + \sin(1.37340)}{3} \approx 1.37406$$
$$x_5 = \dfrac{\pi + \sin(1.37406)}{3} \approx 1.37410$$
$$x_6 = \dfrac{\pi + \sin(1.37410)}{3} \approx 1.37410$$
(Starting with $x_1 = 1$ yields $x_2 \approx 1.32769$, $x_3 \approx 1.37084$, $x_4 \approx 1.37388$, $x_5 \approx 1.37409$, $x_6 \approx 1.37410$).

Verify convergence to 3 decimal places using a sign-change test on $f(x) = 3x - \pi - \sin x$:
$$f(1.3735) = 3(1.3735) - \pi - \sin(1.3735) = 4.1205 - 3.14159 - 0.98064 \approx -0.00173 < 0$$
$$f(1.3745) = 3(1.3745) - \pi - \sin(1.3745) = 4.1235 - 3.14159 - 0.98045 \approx +0.00146 > 0$$
(Note: the official mark scheme printed anomaly records the test interval as $(1.3745, 1.3755)$).

Since the sign change occurs across $1.3735 < x < 1.3745$, round to 3 decimal places:
$$x = 1.374$$
